key_idea: Greedy subsequence matching is optimal, and every block of ten consecutive integers ends in every digit, so the answer is at most about 10n and can be simulated directly.
sketch: Iterate k = 1, 2, ..., write k in decimal and advance a pointer into the target string whenever the current digit matches (standard leftmost-greedy subsequence matching). Stop when the pointer reaches n and print the current k. Since each run of 10 consecutive numbers supplies any wanted digit in the units place, k <= 10n = 1e6, so the simulation is about 7e6 digit steps. Worst case (1e5 zeros) gives k = 207754. Pitfall: the answer is the number being written when the last character is matched, even if matched by a non-final digit.
